Know that regarding the fast itself, there is a great difference between an individual fast and a communal fast. For an individual fast is only a fast of the day, and one does not need to cease eating while it is still day as on Yom Kippur. And it is called a communal fast when one ceases eating while it is still day, but our Sages, of blessed memory, did not treat us stringently in every communal fast to conduct ourselves in this manner, except for Tisha B'Av alone, and likewise for a fast for rain in Eretz Yisrael and during the final fasts, as I have written in siman 575. But for all communal fasts they did not treat us stringently in this, but only as an individual fast. Therefore, when a person accepts a fast, he must say "I am hereby in an individual fast for tomorrow." However, even if he said "fast" without qualification – it is also so (Beit Yosef in siman 563). But if he said "I am hereby in a communal fast for tomorrow" – he ceases eating while it is still day (ibid. and Magen Avraham at the beginning of siman 562).

And our sages, of blessed memory, said in Taanit (12a): Until when may one eat and drink? Until the morning star rises. And this applies both to an individual fast and to a communal fast, with the exception of Tisha B'Av. And even if one ate the evening meal—he may eat more whenever he wishes. However, if he slept a fixed sleep, it is considered an interruption, and he is forbidden from eating. But if he slept a temporary sleep, that is to say, a nap for a short time—he may return and eat. And in the middle of a meal, even if he slept a fixed sleep—he may return and eat, though this is not common. And similarly regarding drinking—some say that it is forbidden when one slept a fixed sleep. And some say that drinking is always permitted, for a person does not divert his mind from drinking. But for eating, a condition is required: that he stipulates that he desires to eat more. And for drinking, he does not require a condition. And such is the custom, because we are accustomed to drink after sleep. And there is one who says that for a fast over a dream—it is forbidden for him to taste anything immediately upon awakening (Magen Avraham). For his remedy is that he should begin to fast immediately. And see what I wrote in siman 288.
